issues.finding: MultiplicativeFiltration is only additive membership with multiplication, antitonicity and 1 in degree 0. It has neither F^0=R, separation, completeness, limits, nor packet operators. The normed-ring theorem cannot certify general inverse-limit-complete filtered algebras, and finite quotient correctness alone does not construct the compatible limit in Lean.
issues.smallest_missing_implication: From the stated separated inverse-limit-complete ideal filtration and compatible finite geometric inverses, construct an element whose images are those inverses and prove both inverse identities by separation.
issues.route: Add exact ideal/quotient inverse-limit completeness data or prove equivalence to a Cauchy-sequence completeness interface. Show geometric partial sums form a compatible quotient family using existing finite telescoping. Lift through the completeness isomorphism and use separation to prove the two residuals zero. Derive weighted word congruence at every L from the existing prunedWordInverse theorem. Add packet support induction and projection continuity to obtain the path block theorem. Do not assume the weighted inverse itself as a completion field.

issues.finding: Completeness of O alone does not make an arbitrary O-algebra B complete for pi^L B. The opening sentence calls this filtration the standard example without imposing completeness on B. The later finite-quotient subsection does not need B complete, but should distinguish that from the completed theorem.
issues.counterexample: For a complete DVR O, B=O[x] is not pi-adically complete: compatible partial sums sum_{j<N} pi^j x^j have no polynomial limit, and 1-pi x is not a unit in O[x]. B=Frac(O) instead has pi^L B=B and is not separated. Neither contradicts the main theorem, whose completeness/separation hypotheses exclude them.
issues.repair: Use B a pi-adically separated and complete O-algebra, for example Mat_d(O) for finite d, when calling the construction a complete filtered example.
